stem.presentation: A 75-year-old woman with non-small cell lung cancer previously treated with chemotherapy and radiation, COPD, and hypertension presents for her third episode of dyspnea and hemoptysis. During an earlier hospitalization, bronchoscopy showed generalized submucosal inflammation without endobronchial lesions or a clear source of injury. During a subsequent admission, she improved with COPD treatment and was discharged with scheduled inhalers and a five-day course of cefpodoxime and azithromycin for community-acquired pneumonia. Her ambulatory oxygen saturation at that discharge was 93–97% on room air. After one day at home, she developed worsening dyspnea after walking back from the bathroom. She reported eating a large meal earlier that evening. Her cough had generally improved, although intermittent rusty sputum persisted. She denied chest pain, palpitations, or diaphoresis. She also reported recent left ankle swelling and pain that improved after taking an unspecified “arthritis pill.” In the ED, she received bronchodilators, methylprednisolone, vancomycin, piperacillin- tazobactam, aspirin, and IV fluids in anticipation of CT angiography. She was subsequently admitted to the hospital floor.

stem.presentation: A 91-year-old woman with diabetes and hypertension presented with two weeks of palpitations, one week of dyspnea, and two days of worsening lower-extremity edema. She was referred to the ED after a home assessment found a heart rate in the 130s. In the ED, her heart rate was in the 140s with a regular narrow-complex tachycardia. IV diltiazem slowed the rate. She received 500 mL of IV fluid while the rhythm was being clarified, then developed an oxygen requirement and received IV furosemide. He denied dyspnea, nausea, vomiting, or diaphoresis. An IV nitroglycerin infusion was titrated with marked improvement in pain; he also received aspirin, morphine, and hydromorphone. dx.text: DIAGNOSIS: Multivessel coronary artery disease requiring CABG.
HF CHARACTERIZATION: HFmrEF, ischemic etiology.

causes.text: CONTRIBUTORS: Chronic stable angina; bilateral leg arterial disease with rest pain; chronic diastolic HF; old MI; hypertensive heart disease with HF.
COMORBIDITIES: Type 2 diabetes with hyperglycemia, hypothyroidism, first-degree AV block, hyperlipidemia, obesity, depression, aortic stenosis, aortic atherosclerosis.

acute.text: START: Oral furosemide — for LV filling pressure >18 mmHg before CABG; titrate to euvolemia; hold if hypotensive or hypovolemic; reduce or hold for overdiuresis or creatinine rise >0.3 mg/dL; reassess need after the SGLT2 inhibitor is started.

gdmt.text: START: Dapagliflozin — hold 3 days before CABG and resume when tolerating oral intake after surgery; hold if eGFR <20; hold with furosemide if creatinine rises >0.3 mg/dL.
START: Spironolactone — hold if K >5.0 or eGFR <30, and perioperatively if K is trending up; no potassium supplements.
START: Clopidogrel — DAPT after recent RCA stent; hold 5 days before CABG and resume afterwards per surgical team; if a PPI is needed use pantoprazole, not omeprazole.
TITRATE DOWN: Aspirin to 81 mg — hold the morning of CABG or if bleeding.

CONTINUE: Lisinopril, metoprolol succinate, high-intensity atorvastatin — hold lisinopril the morning of CABG and if SBP <90, K >5.5 or AKI; hold metoprolol if HR <55 or SBP <90 and do not up-titrate if PR >280 ms or symptomatic bradycardia; continue atorvastatin through surgery.
CONTINUE: U-500 insulin, 225 units morning and 200 units evening with endocrine input — may need reduction after dapagliflozin starts; insulin infusion protocol for CABG.
CONTINUE: Levothyroxine on an empty stomach; venlafaxine, not stopped abruptly, with a coordinated perioperative plan; trazodone.

monitor.text: MONITOR: Renal function and BMP every 3 days while dapagliflozin, furosemide and lisinopril are started together, with daily weights; BMP 3 days and 1 week after starting spironolactone, then weekly; blood glucose four times daily; PR interval on metoprolol; orthostatic BP on trazodone; LFTs if myopathy symptoms.

SAFETY: AKI risk from SGLT2 inhibitor, loop diuretic and ACE inhibitor together; hyperkalemia risk with lisinopril plus spironolactone; omeprazole would weaken clopidogrel; hypoglycemia risk when dapagliflozin is added to high-dose U-500 insulin.
REQUEST: NT-proBNP as an HFmrEF baseline; TSH before CABG; troponin for periprocedural injury after the RCA intervention; ECG after catheterization for new ischemia and a baseline PR interval.

gdmt.text: TITRATE UP: Lisinopril — afterload reduction for severe AR; increase to 20 mg in 1–2 weeks if tolerated, target 20–40 mg; hold if SBP <100 or DBP <50.

START: High-intensity atorvastatin — on the same day pravastatin stops, to avoid statin duplication; reduce to 40 mg for intolerable myalgia or transaminases >3× ULN.
TITRATE DOWN: Aspirin 325 → 81 mg — continue through the preoperative period unless cardiothoracic surgery asks for a hold.

CONTINUE: Clopidogrel — stop now if the DES was placed >12 months ago, otherwise hold 5–7 days before AVR; discuss stent-thrombosis risk with interventional cardiology; alert surgery and anesthesia if urgent surgery follows a hold of <5 days.
CONTINUE: Trazodone, hold for symptomatic orthostasis or SBP <100; inhaled fluticasone.

COMPLICATIONS: Warfarin adverse effect; effusive-constrictive pericarditis; acute kidney injury; pleural effusion; hyperkalemia.

START: Vitamin K 2.5 mg orally once — only if INR remains >3.0 after FFP; recheck INR 6–12 h later and repeat once if still >2.5.

gdmt.text: STOP: Warfarin permanently — supratherapeutic INR caused the hemorrhagic tamponade.

START: Apixaban 5 mg twice daily — only when INR <2.0, the pericardial drain is out, repeat echo shows no reaccumulation and hemostasis has held 48–72 h; never overlap with warfarin; reassess for 2.5 mg if creatinine reaches ≥1.5 or weight is ≤60 kg (2 of 3 criteria needed).

START: Dapagliflozin — hold if eGFR <20.
START: Spironolactone — defer until K <5.0 on 2 consecutive checks and the SGLT2 inhibitor is established (3–5 days); stop if K >5.5 or creatinine >2.5; no potassium supplements.
START: Colchicine for effusive-constrictive pericarditis — hold for diarrhea, WBC <3000 or eGFR <30; avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors.
START: Atorvastatin — consider 20 mg if poorly tolerated.
CONTINUE: Albuterol and ipratropium as needed — by nebulizer, not IV.

STOP: IV ketorolac — no benefit added to ibuprofen; substitute for ibuprofen only if oral is not tolerated.

CONTINUE: Citalopram — switch to sertraline if QTc >500 ms.
CONTINUE: Oxycodone ER and clonazepam at lowest effective doses; taper clonazepam if feasible.
CONTINUE: Verapamil, omeprazole, SQ heparin, docusate, senna, polyethylene glycol; aluminum-magnesium hydroxide-simethicone as needed, 2 h apart from colchicine.

acute.text: START: IV furosemide bolus then continuous infusion — titrate to urine output >100 mL/h; consider adding IV chlorothiazide if response is inadequate.
CONTINUE: Metolazone — sequential nephron blockade, given 30 minutes before the loop dose; hold if Na <128 or K <3.0.
HOLD: Oral torsemide during IV diuresis — resume at discharge, dose adjusted to response and volume status.

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: Spironolactone — no potassium supplement without checking K.
CONTINUE: Metoprolol succinate — reduce to 25 mg if SBP <90, HR <55 or low output; no up-titration during decompensation.
CONTINUE: Hydralazine and isosorbide mononitrate in place of ACEi/ARB/ARNI because of CKD stage 4.
START: Dapagliflozin — only once SBP is consistently >95 and hemodynamics are stable; expect an initial eGFR dip, stop only if eGFR falls >30% or below 20.
CONTINUE: Amiodarone — ventricular arrhythmia suppression; hold if QTc >500 ms.
CONTINUE: Prophylactic SQ heparin until discharge — switch without overlap to therapeutic IV heparin if LV thrombus is confirmed.
START: Warfarin 2.5 mg (reduced from 5 mg for amiodarone) — only if LV thrombus is confirmed; overlap with IV heparin until INR ≥2.0 for ≥24 hours, continue at least 3–6 months with repeat imaging.
STOP: Aspirin — once warfarin is therapeutic; without thrombus or warfarin, may continue pending transplant team input.
CONTINUE: Levothyroxine and omeprazole, at least 4 hours apart; consider stopping omeprazole if aspirin stops.

monitor.text: MONITOR: BMP and potassium every 8 hours during aggressive diuresis, then daily; renal function every 3 days during dapagliflozin initiation; INR every 3 days until stable at 2.0–3.0; TSH and LFTs every 3–6 months on amiodarone.

stem.presentation: A 77-year-old man with ESRD on hemodialysis, COPD and combined HF had bradycardia, hypotension and hypoxemia during dialysis. dx.text: DIAGNOSIS: Symptomatic bradycardia with syncope/cardiac arrest — AF with slow ventricular response during hemodialysis.

causes.text: CONTRIBUTORS: Acute on chronic systolic HF; mitral and tricuspid regurgitation.
COMPLICATIONS: Syncope and collapse; hypokalemia.
COMORBIDITIES: End-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, COPD, cirrhosis, thrombocytopenia, anemia and aortic atherosclerosis.

acute.text: CONTINUE: Dopamine infusion — wean when HR >60 and SBP >90 are sustained; stop after pacemaker implantation.
CONTINUE: Vancomycin (trough-guided, per dialysis protocol) and cefepime (ESRD dosing) for possible sepsis — stop if cultures are negative at 48–72 hours with clinical improvement.
CONTINUE: Sublingual nitroglycerin as needed for chest pain — only if SBP >100, with extreme caution given hypotension on midodrine and dopamine.

gdmt.text: HOLD: Sacubitril-valsartan, spironolactone and dapagliflozin — not started because of anuric ESRD on dialysis, with chronic hypotension against ARNI and interdialytic hyperkalemia risk against MRA; reassess ARNI if hemodynamics improve after CRT.
HOLD: Carvedilol — not started because of symptomatic bradycardia; start at low dose after CRT-P/CRT-D implantation.
HOLD: Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate — not started because of chronic hypotension; start after CRT if SBP stays >100 off midodrine.
CONTINUE: Aspirin and clopidogrel — hold if platelets <50 or bleeding; stop clopidogrel if anticoagulation is started.
CONTINUE: Midodrine — wean if SBP stays >100 after CRT.
STOP: Omeprazole — replaced by pantoprazole (continued) to avoid the clopidogrel interaction.

monitor.text: MONITOR: Magnesium periodically on PPI with ESRD; neurological status on cefepime (consider a cefepime level) and acyclovir; heart rate on salmeterol, reassessed after the pacemaker.
